macosJourney test flow: route(EnterpriseModulesList → pending Promise assigning resolveModules) [131-135]; mountShell; click 'Business' [147]; waitFor('.np-skeleton') [148]; resolveModules([...]) [149]

The harness bridge runs the route handler synchronously inside `invoke` (routes.get(channel) → handler(payload)), so resolveModules is assigned exactly when the renderer calls ipc.enterpriseModules.list()

BusinessView renders <SkeletonLines rows={5}/> (class np-skeleton) on its FIRST render while modules===null (lines 83-90) and only issues ipc.enterpriseModules.list() from a passive effect (useEffect(() => void reload(), [reload]) lines 57-59; reload awaits list() at line 47). The skeleton is therefore in the DOM strictly before the IPC request is made

BusinessView is code-split: AppShell lazy(() => import('@renderer/business/BusinessView')) behind <Suspense fallback={<ViewFallback/>}>; ViewFallback renders NOTHING under LOADING_FLASH_THRESHOLD_MS (useDelayedFlag) and then a Spinner, never an .np-skeleton

Race diagnosis: the first click on Business triggers the FIRST dynamic import of the BusinessView chunk in that vitest worker (isolated module cache per test file). On a fast runner the import resolves inside user.click()'s own awaits and act() scope, so React flushes the passive effect synchronously → list() invoked → resolveModules assigned BEFORE waitFor starts. On a slow Windows runner the import resolves AFTER user.click() returned; the Suspense-resolution commit happens outside act(), React schedules the passive effect as a separate scheduler task, the skeleton insertion satisfies waitFor via MutationObserver (microtask), the test continues to line 149 before the effect runs, and resolveModules is still undefined → TypeError. The test waits on a DOM proxy (.np-skeleton) that BusinessView renders before it asks for data, instead of on the precondition itself (the handler having been invoked)

facts.fact: ui-tests/appNavigationE2E.test.tsx:156-175 carries the identical pattern (deferred resolveModules; waitFor('.np-skeleton'); resolveModules(...)) and is therefore latently racy on slow runners; it passed on windows-latest in the rc.29 run only by timing

Proposed minimal deterministic fix (test-only, no sleeps, no production change): gate on the handler invocation. In macosJourney.test.tsx replace lines 131-135 with `let resolveModules!: ...; const modulesRequested = new Promise<void>((requested) => route(IpcChannel.EnterpriseModulesList, () => new Promise<EnterpriseModuleSummary[]>((r) => { resolveModules = r; requested(); })));` and insert `await modulesRequested;` between the skeleton waitFor (line 148) and `resolveModules([financeModule()])` (line 149). Equivalent one-liner: insert `await waitFor(() => expect(resolveModules).toBeTypeOf('function'));` before line 149. Apply the same to appNavigationE2E.test.tsx before line 175. Rejected alternative: pre-warming the lazy chunk via `await import('@renderer/business/BusinessView')` in beforeAll (works, but removes the Suspense phase from what the test exercises)

architecture_invariant_notes: Distribution/signing is orthogonal to the authority chain: the Windows client remains a compute/observation surface; no Windows-specific code path grants authorization (F065 shows only cosmetic/platform branches).

Update path: an unsigned, unverified update (F062) would let a network host (the feed) become an implicit authority over what code runs on Computer-B — a 'network connection implies authorization' exposure in the supply chain rather than in the product's decision path. Signing + publisherName closes it.

The feed sha512 check (verify-release-artifacts + electron-updater) is an integrity control, not an authenticity control; stale-authorization rejection (allowDowngrade=false) is in place for versions but not for feed provenance.
